facts.fact: SAPS told the Portfolio Committee on Police on 4 May 2021 that the Integrated Case Docket Management System (ICDMS) had been implemented in 998 police stations with 159 still to be covered, a total of 1 157 by addition (the same meeting's plan counts 1 156 stations); stated by Lt Gen Mfazi, Deputy National Commissioner: Crime Detection, and repeated by Maj Gen Mavundla, Head: Technology Management, in answer to a question about the position at the end of 2020/21.

SAPS's Head of Technology Management told the Portfolio Committee on Police on 4 May 2021 that at the 159 police stations without ICDMS, cases were registered on the old system, which merged the information into the same database as ICDMS; those stations were to receive ICDMS as the network was upgraded.
facts.system: the old system (unnamed; predecessor of ICDMS)

facts.fact: SAPS told the Portfolio Committee on Police on 4 May 2021 that cases are registered and processed on ICDMS at the police stations where it is implemented, and on the old system at the rest.

SAPS's Head of Technology Management told the Portfolio Committee on Police on 4 May 2021 that ICDMS depends on the station's network link, low network hampering the processing of cases, and that cases registered on the old system at the other stations are merged into the same database as ICDMS.

SAPS told the Portfolio Committee on Police on 4 May 2021 that its Technology Management Services was engaging SITA over technical difficulties with ICDMS at the remaining stations, and that there were external parties to the project.
